compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
All seven rows use the same handover records, requirements, deadline, and decision authority.

Either person can consider both columns. Mandatory requirements apply in every example. The table separates information, decision criteria, and arrangements.

| Same handover, information, and authority | INTJ: possible emphasis | ISFP: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reviewing reports that may describe the same issue | What patterns across the entries suggest about a possible shared cause | Which locations, conditions, and measurements the entries actually document | S/N: possible connections and recorded details |
| Prioritizing the same optional improvement | How does it rank when the same priority and cost criteria apply to all options? | How much would it improve the experience of the people who use the equipment? | T/F: consistently applied criteria and impact on people. Mandatory items are handled separately. |
| Considering an exception to the same optional practice | Would the same exception criteria apply in comparable cases? | How would granting or denying it affect the people who use the equipment? | T/F: consistent standards and effects on people. Either person can consider both. |

Shared Introversion is about where attention and energy tend to go. It does not establish how much someone says or when they speak.

The three differences can vary independently. Someone can rely on concrete measurements and weigh how a decision affects people. The same person can make a provisional plan for one decision and keep options open for another.

- **S/N concerns information.** Compare documented details and relevant experience with connections and possibilities.

### INTJ and ISFP: twenty-seven snag items, and what the sorting rests on

In this fictional handover, two reviewers have the same 27 reported issues, inspection records, deadline, and authority. Both are trying to determine which records describe the same issue and which need separate review.

One way to read the records is to look for patterns across entries that may point to a common cause. Another is to compare the documented location, measurement, and observation for each entry. Either reviewer can use both approaches.

A recurring pattern is a lead to investigate. A measurement can confirm what happened in one place without establishing a cause. Use both to decide which entries can be reviewed together.

**Fictional example.** The counts illustrate how to keep the original reports and a grouped review list traceable. They are not acceptance or safety criteria.

In the fictional handover, the client logged five reports about one closure, three about the same door, and three observations that still need verification. Both reviewers can check those groups against the original records.

If the authorized reviewer treats each of the three groups as one review item, the list goes from 27 original reports to 19 review items. The example separates six items referred for mandatory or safety review, nine concerning everyday operation, and four concerning appearance. Keep the original report, grouped review item, and agreed action in separate fields. Whether any item can be closed or deferred requires the applicable procedures and authorization.

Records can cite the relevant requirement, the observed impact, and the evidence still needed. Report counts or tone alone cannot establish severity. Either type can reference the requirements or document a specific condition.

### INTJ and ISFP: same four names, two seats out of place

Both types are introverted, so the auxiliary process faces outward in type dynamics. INTJ’s J indicates auxiliary extraverted Thinking (Te), supporting dominant introverted Intuition (Ni). ISFP’s P indicates auxiliary extraverted Sensing (Se), supporting dominant introverted Feeling (Fi).

In this notation, Ni–Te–Fi–Se for INTJ becomes Fi–Se–Ni–Te for ISFP. Ni moves between dominant and tertiary, Te between auxiliary and inferior, and Fi and Se move in the other direction. These positions do not assign anyone to negotiate or inspect.

The Foundation lists tertiary Feeling for INTJ (Fe or Fi) and tertiary Intuition for ISFP (Ne or Ni). This page uses Fi and Ni. The full four-process overlap applies to this notation. Read more in the [INTJ profile](/en/personality/intj) and [ISFP profile](/en/personality/isfp).

In this fictional handover, two reviewers have the same 27 reported issues, inspection records, deadline, and authority. Both are trying to determine which records describe the same issue and which need separate review.

One way to read the records is to look for patterns across entries that may point to a common cause. Another is to compare the documented location, measurement, and observation for each entry. Either reviewer can use both approaches.

A recurring pattern is a lead to investigate. A measurement can confirm what happened in one place without establishing a cause. Use both to decide which entries can be reviewed together.

Both types are introverted, so the auxiliary process faces outward in type dynamics. INTJ’s J indicates auxiliary extraverted Thinking (Te), supporting dominant introverted Intuition (Ni). ISFP’s P indicates auxiliary extraverted Sensing (Se), supporting dominant introverted Feeling (Fi).
